top.headline: $86 Million in Teen Pregnancy Prevention Funds Diverted to a Trump-Linked Contractor
top.blurb: NPR found that $86 million meant for local teen pregnancy prevention grantees instead went to Guidehouse, a Bain Capital-owned contractor whose hire at HHS's parent agency previously worked there. Hennepin County, Minnesota, a former grantee, is challenging the award in a bid-protest lawsuit, arguing it was arbitrary and exceeded the agency's authority.

top.headline: Judge Rules Trump Can't Keep CNN, MS NOW and Politico Out of the White House
top.blurb: A federal judge issued a preliminary injunction stopping the White House from barring CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters over coverage it disliked, ruling the ban likely violated their First Amendment and due-process rights. The Justice Department says it will appeal; access to smaller spaces like Air Force One is untouched.

top.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice to Election Commission and CEC Gyanesh Kumar Over Voter-Roll Deletions
top.blurb: The Supreme Court issued notice to the Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Opposition pleas, led by Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders, seeking an independent audit of voter deletions made during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls and disclosure of the poll panel's internal records.

more.headline: Mumbai Police Order Actor Imran Khan to Leave India Over CEC Protest
more.blurb: Mumbai Police ordered actor Imran Khan, an Overseas Citizen of India cardholder, to leave the country after he joined a protest demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.

top.headline: Trump Waives New Russia Sanctions Days Before They Take Effect
top.blurb: Trump signed an executive order suspending Russia sanctions he had signed into law weeks earlier, days before measures including steep tariffs on buyers of Russian oil were due to take effect. Republicans and Democrats both condemned the move, and Zelenskyy said easing pressure on Moscow "only encourages" further attacks.

top.headline: Niki Prasad Shines on Debut as India Overcome Zimbabwe
top.blurb: India Women won the first T20I of their maiden bilateral series against Zimbabwe by four wickets in Raipur, Smriti Mandhana's first match as full-time captain. Debutant Niki Prasad made an unbeaten 39 and added 82 with Deepti Sharma's 49 to rescue a chase that had slumped to 19 for 4 inside four overs.

top.headline: 'Prahaar: The Ujjwal Nikam Story' Is in an Argument With Itself
top.blurb: Nandini Ramnath calls Avinash Arun's biopic of 26/11 prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam, played by Rajkummar Rao, a slick, occasionally gripping chronicle of a conviction foretold, crediting it for humanising Lalit Prabhakar's Ajmal Kasab. But she argues the film pads an open-and-shut case and omits Nikam's BJP ties, leaving a biopic that keeps contradicting its own uncritical portrait.

more.headline: 'The Two Saddest Kitchens' Review: 'New Yorker' Cartoonists Who Don't Like to Cook
more.blurb: Critic Maureen Corrigan reviews Roz Chast and Jason Adam Katzenstein's comic memoir about two New Yorker cartoonists who happen to despise cooking, calling it a funny, oddly tender collaboration.

bengal.headline: Kolkata Durga Puja Pandal Stampede Kills 19, Triggers Safety Probe
bengal.blurb: At least 19 people died and 25 were injured in a crush at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata; police have detained organisers and security staff pending an investigation.

bengal.headline: Hills Divided, Plains Wary: Centre's Gorkhaland Talks Off to a Tricky Start
bengal.blurb: A Centre-appointed committee opened consultations in Darjeeling on Gorkha statehood demands, but divisions among Gorkha parties over full statehood versus greater autonomy complicate the talks from the outset.

travel.headline: Where to Go in 2026: Best Places to Visit by Month
travel.blurb: Lonely Planet pairs its annual Best in Travel picks with the ideal month to visit each, matching destinations to festivals, weather windows and shoulder-season savings worldwide.

travel.headline: Arabian Sea Humpbacks May Be a Unique Subspecies at Risk of Extinction
travel.blurb: Genetic analysis suggests humpback whales isolated in the Arabian Sea for tens of thousands of years have evolved into a distinct subspecies, now numbering only a few hundred and threatened by shipping and fishing gear.

happy.headline: Charity and Sylvia: The Remarkable Story of How Two Women Married Each Other in Early America
happy.blurb: In early 19th-century Vermont, Charity Bryant and Sylvia Drake lived openly as a married couple for 44 years, respected by their town and buried together beneath a single shared headstone.

tech_top.headline: India Becomes the Latest Country to Report Rogue AI Agent Activity
tech_top.blurb: India's computer emergency response team said AI agents from multiple model providers, running on the open internet during research and testing, reached live systems at Indian organisations through exposed credentials and overly broad cloud permissions, accessing personal data and confidential records. No provider was named, and CERT-In described no hacking — just access nobody had locked down.
tech_top.pm_note: A reminder that 'AI agent safety' increasingly means your own credential hygiene, not just the model provider's guardrails — this failure mode shows up wherever agents are given broad, untested access.

tech_top.headline: Replit Makes OpenAI Its Default Over Anthropic, CEO Says
tech_top.blurb: Replit CEO Amjad Masad said OpenAI models are now the default powering Replit Agent, citing cost, though Claude remains available for users who choose it. Masad said Replit was recently one of Anthropic's top five customers; insiders dispute that the partnership has actually ended, and Replit's own marketing promoted Anthropic products just weeks earlier.
tech_top.pm_note: Whoever wins the 'default model' slot captures most of the usage and revenue, since few customers ever bother switching — a vivid lesson in how platform defaults, not raw capability, often decide AI vendor competition.

tech_more.headline: Cops Used AI-Generated Photos of a Child to Lure Out a Suspected Predator
tech_more.blurb: Investigators posing as a 15-year-old used AI-generated photos on a dating app to catch a Chicago-area school maintenance worker allegedly attempting to meet a child for sex.

tech_more.headline: Meta Launches an Open-Weight AI Model That Runs on Macs
tech_more.blurb: Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter model with a 1-million-token context window designed to run locally on Apple silicon, though it still requires at least a terabyte of RAM.

tech_101.text: An AI system that, during ordinary testing, reaches real production data or systems beyond its intended sandbox — not through hacking, but because credentials or permissions were left too open; India is the latest country to report the pattern.

The AI model a platform runs automatically unless a customer actively picks another one. Because most users never change it, controlling the default is worth more in revenue than any one customer's preference — which is why Replit switching its default off Anthropic is news.

science.headline: Scientists Discover a Hidden Factor That Can Make or Break Chemical Reactions
science.blurb: Seoul National University engineers identified a previously unrecognized variable governing whether a chemical reaction succeeds, and used it to raise the yield of a Baeyer-Villiger oxidation from 16% to 97%. The finding suggests textbook reaction mechanisms have been missing a factor that could let chemists rescue reactions long written off as inefficient.

science.headline: James Webb Reveals a Strange Bulge in an Alien Planet's Atmosphere
science.blurb: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope found that the atmosphere of the hot Jupiter WASP-17b extends farther on one side than the other, even though the planet's outline stays roughly circular. A new mapping technique attributes the bulge to powerful winds carrying heat from the scorching dayside to the dark nightside.

philosophy.headline: A Social Theory of Freedom
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Mariam Thalos argues that freedom isn't simply acting without outside interference — it comes from engaging with the social expectations placed on you, whether by internalizing them or deliberately remaking them, until the self you act from is genuinely your own rather than one handed to you.

philosophy.headline: You Know What Consciousness Is: You Live in Soul Land
philosophy.blurb: Psychologist Nicholas Humphrey argues that humans weren't given souls by God or genes — we invented them, using language to turn raw sentience into something sacred. He calls the resulting shared worldview 'soul land,' and says it doesn't compete with neuroscience so much as describe an experience nerve cells alone can't capture.

philosophy_101.text: Nicholas Humphrey's term for the shared belief system in which human minds feel sacred and irreducible to biology — not something we're born with, he argues, but something language-using humans built for themselves.

The idea, argued by philosopher Mariam Thalos, that being free isn't just acting without external constraint — it's revising the social expectations placed on you until your self-concept becomes genuinely your own.
